items.title: 1.2 Equality of Two Complex Numbers (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Is sabaq mein hum seekhenge ke do complex numbers kab "barabar" kehlate hain, aur is chhote se rule se ek hi equation mein se do unknowns kaise nikalte hain. Pichle sabaq (1.1) mein aap ne parha tha ke har complex number \(a + bi\) ke do hisse (parts) hote hain: real part \(a\) aur imaginary part \(b\). Ab hum isi baat ko istemal karenge.

Pehle real numbers ki baat karte hain. Do real numbers barabar tab hote hain jab woh ek hi number hon, jaise \(5 = 5\). Wahan sirf ek cheez compare karni hoti hai. Lekin complex number ke andar do cheezein hain, is liye humein ek saaf rule chahiye. Kitab yeh rule deti hai: do complex numbers \(z_{1} = a + bi\) aur \(z_{2} = c + di\) tab aur sirf tab (iff) barabar hain jab un ke real parts barabar hon aur imaginary parts bhi barabar hon, yani

blocks.latex: a + bi = c + di \iff a = c \ \text{and}\ b = d
blocks.text_alt: a plus b i equals c plus d i if and only if a equals c and b equals d

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
"iff" ka matlab hai "if and only if" (agar aur sirf agar). Yani rule dono taraf chalta hai: agar dono parts barabar hain to numbers barabar hain, aur agar numbers barabar hain to dono parts zaroor barabar honge.
Ek misaal se samajhiye. Socheiye aap ka dost kehta hai "mera ghar Gali number 3 aur Makan number 2 par hai". Agar kisi aur ka pata bhi Gali 3, Makan 2 ho, tabhi dono ek hi ghar hain. Sirf gali same ho aur makan alag ho to ghar alag hai. Bilkul isi tarah \(a + bi\) ko Argand diagram par point \((a, b)\) samjhein: do points tabhi ek hi jagah hote hain jab un ke dono coordinates same hon.
Is rule ki asal taqat yeh hai: ek complex equation se humein do real equations mil jati hain. Is liye ek hi equation se do unknowns (jaise \(x\) aur \(y\)) find ho sakte hain, jo real numbers mein mumkin nahin hota.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text:
Compare karne se pehle dono sides ko (real part) + (imaginary part)\(i\) ki shakal mein le aana zaroori hai. Jab tak koi side brackets mein band hai ya us mein \(i^{2}\) para hai, tab tak compare mat karein.
Chhoti si misaal dekhiye: \(x + 3i = 7 - yi\). Left side ka real part \(x\) hai aur right side ka \(7\), is liye \(x = 7\). Left side ka imaginary part \(3\) hai aur right side ka \(-y\), is liye \(3 = -y\), yani \(y = -3\).
Khud sochiye: agar \(2x + 4i = 10 + yi\) ho to \(x\) aur \(y\) kya honge? (Jawab: \(x = 5\), \(y = 4\).)

Ab kitab ki misaal dekhte hain. Is mein left side seedhi (real) + (imaginary)\(i\) ki shakal mein nahin hai; pehle humein multiply karna parega. Dhyan se har step dekhiye, kyun ke Exercise 1.2 ke kai sawal bilkul isi tarah hal hote hain.

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.problem: If \((3+2i)(x+iy) = 5+12i\), where \(x, y \in \mathbb{R}\), then find the values of \(x\) and \(y\).
steps:
Given: \((3+2i)(x+iy) = 5+12i\), aur \(x, y\) real numbers hain.
To find: \(x\) aur \(y\) ki values.
Method: sab se pehle hum yeh samajhte hain ke sawal kya chahta hai: do unknowns, lekin equation sirf ek. Real numbers mein ek equation se do unknowns nahin nikalte, magar yahan equation complex hai. Hum left side ko multiply kar ke (real part) + (imaginary part)\(i\) ki shakal mein likhenge, phir equality ka rule lagayenge: real = real aur imaginary = imaginary. Is tarah do aam equations ban jayengi, jinhein hum simultaneous equations (ek saath hal hone wali equations) ki tarah hal karenge.

Step 1: Left side ko multiply karein
\[(3+2i)(x+iy)\]
\[= 3x + 3iy + 2ix + 2yi^{2}\]
Kyun: pehli bracket ka har term doosri bracket ke har term se multiply hota hai, bilkul \((a+b)(c+d) = ac + ad + bc + bd\) ki tarah. Yahan \(3 \cdot x = 3x\), \(3 \cdot iy = 3iy\), \(2i \cdot x = 2ix\) aur \(2i \cdot iy = 2yi^{2}\). Chaar terms aani chahiye; agar aap ke paas teen hain to koi term reh gaya hai.

Step 2: \(i^{2} = -1\) lagayein aur parts ko ikattha karein
\[2yi^{2} = 2y(-1) = -2y\]
\[(3x - 2y) + (2x + 3y)i = 5 + 12i\]
Kyun: \(i^{2} = -1\) hai, is liye \(2yi^{2}\) ab imaginary nahin raha balke real term \(-2y\) ban gaya. Ab jin terms mein \(i\) nahin, unhein ek jagah jama kiya: \(3x - 2y\) real part hai. Jin terms mein \(i\) hai, un ka coefficient (\(i\) ke saath laga number) \(2x + 3y\) imaginary part hai.
Dhyan dein: bohat se students yahan \(2yi^{2}\) ko imaginary part mein daal dete hain kyun ke us mein "i" nazar aa raha hai. Yaad rakhiye, \(i^{2}\) koi imaginary cheez nahin, yeh seedha \(-1\) hai.

Step 3: Real aur imaginary parts ko compare karein
\[3x - 2y = 5 \quad \text{...(i)}\]
\[2x + 3y = 12 \quad \text{...(ii)}\]
Kyun: yahi is topic ka asal rule hai. Do complex numbers tabhi barabar hote hain jab dono ke real parts barabar hon aur imaginary parts bhi barabar hon. Left ka real part \(3x - 2y\) right ke real part \(5\) ke barabar, aur left ka imaginary part \(2x + 3y\) right ke imaginary part \(12\) ke barabar. Ghor karein: hum \(12\) likhte hain, \(12i\) nahin, kyun ke imaginary part sirf coefficient hota hai.

Step 4: \(y\) wali terms ko ulta (opposite) banayein
Equation (i) ko 3 se aur equation (ii) ko 2 se multiply karein:
\[9x - 6y = 15\]
\[4x + 6y = 24\]
Kyun: ab humare paas do aam equations hain, aur inhein elimination method (ek variable khatam karne ka tareeqa) se hal karna aasan hai. Hum chahte hain ke \(y\) ke coefficients barabar magar ulte sign wale hon. \(-2y\) aur \(3y\) ka LCM 6 hai, is liye (i) ko 3 se aur (ii) ko 2 se multiply kiya: ab \(-6y\) aur \(+6y\) hain. Yaad rakhiye, equation ko multiply karte waqt dono sides ke har term ko multiply karna hai (\(5 \times 3 = 15\), \(12 \times 2 = 24\)).

Step 5: Dono equations jama karein
\[9x - 6y + 4x + 6y = 15 + 24\]
\[13x = 39\]
\[x = 3\]
Kyun: jama karne se \(-6y\) aur \(+6y\) aapas mein khatam ho gaye, aur sirf \(x\) wali ek equation bachi. Phir dono sides ko 13 se divide kiya to \(x = 3\) mil gaya.

Step 6: \(y\) find karein
\(x = 3\) ko \(9x - 6y = 15\) mein rakhein (yeh equation (i) hi hai jo 3 se multiply hui thi; kitab yahi use karti hai):
\[9(3) - 6y = 15\]
\[27 - 6y = 15\]
\[-6y = -12\]
\[y = 2\]
Kyun: jab ek unknown maloom ho jaye to \(y\) wali koi bhi equation \(y\) de deti hai. \(27\) ko right side le gaye to \(15 - 27 = -12\) bana, phir \(-6\) se divide kiya. Agar aap seedha (i) mein rakhein: \(3(3) - 2y = 5\), yani \(9 - 2y = 5\), phir bhi \(y = 2\) hi aata hai. Dono raaste ek hi jawab dete hain, yeh bhi ek chhoti si tasdeeq hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(x = 3\), \(y = 2\) rakhne se \(x + iy = 3 + 2i\) banta hai. Ab left side dobara nikaalte hain:
\[(3+2i)(3+2i) = 9 + 6i + 6i + 4i^{2}\]
\[= 9 + 12i - 4 = 5 + 12i\]
Yeh wahi right side hai jo sawal mein di gayi thi, is liye jawab bilkul durust hai. Exam mein yeh check sirf aadha minute leta hai magar ghalti pakar leta hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ek aur chhoti misaal khud kar ke dekhiye (yeh kitab ka sawal nahin, hamari practice hai): agar \((1 + i)(x + iy) = 2 + 4i\) ho to?
Multiply karein: \(x + iy + ix + i^{2}y = (x - y) + (x + y)i\).
Compare karein: \(x - y = 2\) aur \(x + y = 4\).
Jama karein: \(2x = 6\), yani \(x = 3\); phir \(y = 1\).
Tasdeeq: \((1 + i)(3 + i) = 3 + i + 3i + i^{2} = 2 + 4i\). Bilkul sahi!

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(a + bi = c + di\) tabhi jab \(a = c\) aur \(b = d\); rule dono taraf chalta hai (iff).
2. Ek complex equation = do real equations: ek real parts ki, ek imaginary parts ki.
3. Tarteeb yaad rakhiye: pehle multiply/simplify, phir \(i^{2} = -1\), phir (real) + (imaginary)\(i\) ki shakal, aur aakhir mein compare.
4. Do equations ko elimination ya substitution se hal karein.
5. Aakhir mein jawab asal equation mein rakh kar tasdeeq zaroor karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(i^{2} = -1\) bhool jana: \(2yi^{2}\) real term hai (\(-2y\)); yeh imaginary part mein nahin jata. Bachne ka tareeqa: multiply karte hi har \(i^{2}\) ko foran \(-1\) se badal dein.
2. \(2x + 3y\) ko \(12i\) ke barabar likh dena: imaginary part sirf \(i\) ka coefficient hota hai, yani \(12\), \(12i\) nahin.
3. Simplify kiye baghair compare kar dena, jaise brackets khole baghair "3 = 5" likh dena. Pehle poori side ko \(a + bi\) ki shakal mein laayein.
4. Terms idhar udhar karte waqt sign ki ghalti; is liye jawab ko asal equation mein rakh kar check karein.
